title: The Widening Gap
text:
Economic inequality has grown markedly in many developed nations over the past four decades. Researchers attribute this trend to a combination of technological change, weakening labour unions and tax policies that favour capital over wages. Although overall prosperity has increased, the benefits have accrued disproportionately to the wealthiest households. As a result, social mobility has stagnated for many families born into modest circumstances.

Some economists argue that moderate inequality is an unavoidable by-product of innovation, since entrepreneurs must be rewarded for taking risks. Others contend that extreme disparities undermine public trust and weaken democratic participation. Policymakers therefore face a delicate balance between encouraging growth and ensuring that opportunity is not confined to a privileged minority. The debate, unsurprisingly, remains deeply polarised.

questions.text: To what do researchers attribute the trend of growing inequality?
options: Technological change and weakening labour unions
Rising birth rates among the wealthy

questions.text: According to some economists, why is moderate inequality unavoidable?
options: Entrepreneurs must be rewarded for taking risks
Wages have been frozen for decades

questions.text: What can be inferred about families born into modest circumstances?
options: They have benefited most from recent prosperity
They are more likely to become entrepreneurs than the wealthy
They generally experience little upward movement between generations
They rarely take part in democratic processes

questions.text: What does the author's final sentence suggest about the debate over inequality?
options: It will be quickly resolved by new evidence
It is unlikely to reach a consensus soon
It is limited to academic circles

paragraph_translations: A desigualdade econômica cresceu de forma acentuada em muitas nações desenvolvidas nas últimas quatro décadas. Os pesquisadores atribuem essa tendência a uma combinação de mudanças tecnológicas, do enfraquecimento dos sindicatos e de políticas tributárias que favorecem o capital em detrimento dos salários. Embora a prosperidade geral tenha aumentado, os benefícios se acumularam de forma desproporcional entre as famílias mais ricas. Como resultado, a mobilidade social estagnou para muitas famílias nascidas em circunstâncias modestas.

Alguns economistas argumentam que a desigualdade moderada é um subproduto inevitável da inovação, já que os empreendedores precisam ser recompensados por assumir riscos. Outros sustentam que disparidades extremas minam a confiança pública e enfraquecem a participação democrática. Os formuladores de políticas, portanto, enfrentam um equilíbrio delicado entre estimular o crescimento e garantir que as oportunidades não fiquem restritas a uma minoria privilegiada. O debate, como era de se esperar, permanece profundamente polarizado.
